leverage.exposure: The balance is negative and will stay negative until the Gregoritsch sale executes. That is deliberate and currently harmless: a deficit costs nothing until the instant the matchday locks, and the lock is roughly three days away. The single sale unwinds it in one move with room to spare, so there is no sequencing risk and no second leg to arrange. binding_gap: Goalkeeper, and it has not moved. Neuer is the only keeper in the squad and he is carrying a status flag, so a late ruling against him means fielding ten and taking the penalty. movers.reason: No qualifying flip. This is a timing kill, not an absence of the mechanism — the tick edge itself is intact and has not decayed for a ninth consecutive run. Every rising Kickbase board listing on the market expires after tonight's update, which means winning one buys at the post-tick price and bets on a flag that will be re-read before it resolves. Simpson-Pusey expires precisely at the tick, which is not before it, and he was already killed on an earlier run. The more important thing is the losing streak. Both legs tonight were bid at exactly market value and both were lost, making five consecutive auctions lost at that bid, and the winning premiums are trending up rather than scattering — the ladder now runs from low single digits to nearly nineteen percent. The drift is not the problem; entry is. An edge that never executes is worth nothing, and bidding at market value puts us last in the queue behind anyone willing to pay a euro more. The honest answer is that this needs a decision from Georg rather than another two-hourly log entry, and the arithmetic cuts against the obvious fix: a small premium entry roughly cancels a single tick, so paying up is a different trade with a multi-day hold and different risk, not a tweak to this one. Recommendation for now: keep bidding exactly market value, keep logging the ladder, and treat the rule as under review.
